title: Silicon Valley Bank: $40 Billion Gone in One Day
summary:
Silicon Valley Bank collapse explained from regulator records.
On 9 March 2023, customers withdrew more than $40 billion from Silicon Valley Bank in a single day; the next day it was closed. Using the Federal Reserve's 2023 review, its inspector general, the FDIC and a new 2026 independent review, we trace what went wrong, who saw it coming, and who paid.
sources: Federal Reserve Board, Review of the Federal Reserve's Supervision and Regulation of Silicon Valley Bank (28 Apr 2023): https://www.federalreserve.gov/publications/files/svb-review-20230428.pdf
Federal Reserve Board, Executive Summary of the review (28 Apr 2023): https://www.federalreserve.gov/publications/2023-April-SVB-Executive-Summary.htm
Federal Reserve Board press release on the review's results (28 Apr 2023): https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/pressreleases/bcreg20230428a.htm
Joint Statement by Treasury, Federal Reserve and FDIC (12 Mar 2023): https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/pressreleases/monetary20230312b.htm
FDIC, First-Citizens Bank & Trust to assume all deposits and loans of Silicon Valley Bridge Bank (Mar 2023): https://www.fdic.gov/news/press-releases/2023/pr23023.html
FDIC, Final Rule on Special Assessment Pursuant to Systemic Risk Determination (Nov 2023): https://www.fdic.gov/news/press-releases/2023/pr23092.html
Federal Reserve OIG, Material Loss Review of Silicon Valley Bank, summary (25 Sep 2023): https://oig.federalreserve.gov/reports/board-material-loss-review-silicon-valley-bank-summary-sep2023.pdf
Speech by Fed Vice Chair for Supervision Michelle Bowman on initial findings from the independent review of SVB (18 Sep 2026): https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/speech/bowman20260918b.htm

scenes.say: On the ninth of March 2023, customers pulled more than 40 billion dollars out of Silicon Valley Bank. In a single day.

visual.text: $40 billion withdrawn in one day
visual.src: Federal Reserve review, executive summary, Apr 2023

scenes.say: The next morning, its managers expected more than 100 billion dollars to follow. Together, that was roughly 85 per cent of all its deposits.

visual.label: Expected to leave the next day
visual.sub: With 9 March: roughly 85% of the deposit base
visual.src: Federal Reserve review, executive summary, Apr 2023

scenes.say: On the tenth of March, California's financial regulator closed it. A banking group with about 212 billion dollars of assets had lost its bank, two days after announcing a plan to raise money.

visual.text: California regulator closes Silicon Valley Bank
visual.src: Federal Reserve review, executive summary, Apr 2023

scenes.say: This was not a small lender. It had tripled in size in two years. And about 94 per cent of its deposits were uninsured.

visual.src: Federal Reserve review, Apr 2023

scenes.say: So how does a group that size run out of money in two days? And who saw it coming?

visual.text: How does a $212bn bank group fail in two days?

scenes.say: The newest official review says supervisors knew, or should have known, about its weaknesses as early as March 2022. A full year before the run.

visual.title: Preliminary findings
lines: !Staff knew, or should have known, about these vulnerabilities as early as March 2022
Staff did not take prompt and decisive action
visual.src: Fed Vice Chair Bowman on independent review, Sep 2026

scenes.say: This is the story of Silicon Valley Bank, told from the regulators' own records.

visual.text: Silicon Valley Bank
visual.sub: Told from the regulators' own records

scenes.say: Silicon Valley Bank was founded in 1983, and was based in Santa Clara, California.

visual.text: The start-up bank

scenes.say: At the end of its first year, it had about 18 million dollars of assets.

visual.label: Assets at the end of 1983
visual.src: Federal Reserve review, Apr 2023

scenes.say: It built its business around one kind of customer: technology and life-sciences companies, many of them young start-ups backed by venture capital.

visual.title: Who banked with SVB
visual.src: Federal Reserve review, Apr 2023

scenes.say: That focus was its strength. But it also meant its customers had a great deal in common. The Federal Reserve later described the client base as heavily concentrated.

visual.text: heavily concentrated in venture capital-backed (VC-backed) and early-stage start-up firms
visual.src: Federal Reserve review, Apr 2023

scenes.say: Then the money poured in. Between 2019 and 2021, the group's assets grew from 71 billion dollars to 211 billion.

visual.title: SVB Financial Group: total assets
visual.src: Federal Reserve review, Apr 2023

scenes.say: From April 2020 to the end of 2021, its deposits grew at an annual rate of about 89 per cent.

visual.label: Annual deposit growth rate
visual.src: Federal Reserve review, Apr 2023

scenes.say: A bank cannot leave deposits sitting idle. It lends them out, or invests them, so that it earns more than it pays its customers.

visual.title: What a bank does with deposits
items: Keeps some as cash for withdrawals

scenes.say: Silicon Valley Bank made an unusual choice about where to put its money.

visual.text: Where did the money go?

scenes.say: By the end of 2022, securities made up 55 per cent of the group's total assets.

visual.text: The bet on bonds

scenes.say: At large banking organisations, the typical share was about 25 per cent. Silicon Valley Bank's was more than double.

visual.title: Securities as a share of total assets, end of 2022
visual.src: Federal Reserve review, Apr 2023

scenes.say: And 78 per cent of those securities were classed as held to maturity: long-dated bonds the bank intended to keep until they paid out.

visual.label: of its securities were held to maturity
visual.src: Federal Reserve review, Apr 2023

scenes.say: Long-dated bonds have a weakness. When interest rates rise, new bonds pay more, so older bonds that pay less lose value.

visual.text: Rates go up. Old bond prices go down.

scenes.say: As interest rates rose in 2022, the Federal Reserve's review found the group saw a rapid increase in unrealized losses on its bond portfolios.

visual.text: SVBFG saw a rapid increase in unrealized losses on both its HTM and available-for-sale (AFS) portfolios
visual.src: Federal Reserve review, Apr 2023

scenes.say: An unrealized loss only becomes real if you have to sell. As long as depositors stayed, the bank could wait.

visual.text: A paper loss. Until you have to sell.

scenes.say: There was also an accounting detail. The review notes that if unrealized losses on its available-for-sale bonds had been counted, the group's regulatory capital at the end of 2022 would have been 1.9 billion dollars lower.

visual.label: Lower regulatory capital, end of 2022
visual.sub: If unrealized losses on available-for-sale bonds had been counted
visual.src: Federal Reserve review, Apr 2023

scenes.say: But the bank also changed how it measured the danger. The review says it made counterintuitive modelling assumptions about how long deposits would stay. And it removed interest-rate hedges that would have protected it against rising rates.

visual.title: Risk management
lines: !Counterintuitive modeling assumptions about the duration of deposits
!Removed interest rate hedges that would have protected against rising interest rates
visual.src: Federal Reserve review, Apr 2023

scenes.say: Meanwhile, the review found, senior managers' pay through 2022 was tied to short-term earnings and equity returns, and did not include risk metrics.

visual.text: Compensation packages of senior management through 2022 were tied to short-term earnings and equity returns and did not include risk metrics.
visual.src: Federal Reserve review, Apr 2023

scenes.say: The Fed's inspector general later summed up the pattern: management emphasised growth, and failed to put in place the controls needed to manage the risks.

visual.text: Its management emphasized growth and failed to implement the controls necessary to effectively mitigate the risks
visual.src: Federal Reserve OIG, Sep 2023

scenes.say: The losses were real, even if they were unrealized. The preliminary findings of a later independent review say that they exceeded the bank's capital.

visual.text: real but unrealized accounting losses on its securities portfolio that exceeded its capital
visual.by: Independent review (preliminary), per Michelle Bowman, Sep 2026
visual.src: Fed Vice Chair Bowman on independent review, Sep 2026

scenes.say: Silicon Valley Bank was supervised by the Federal Reserve, through the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco.

visual.text: The warnings

scenes.say: In 2021, it was moved into the Fed's portfolio for large banking organisations. The San Francisco Fed's team watching it grew from about eight people to 20.

visual.src: Federal Reserve review, executive summary, Apr 2023

scenes.say: But the inspector general found that the supervisory approach had not evolved with the bank's growth, and that the move to the large-bank portfolio was not handled effectively.

visual.text: the RBO supervisory approach for SVB did not evolve with SVB's growth and increased complexity.
visual.src: Federal Reserve OIG, Sep 2023

scenes.say: Supervisors did find problems. When the bank failed, it had 31 open supervisory findings. That was about triple the number at peer firms.

visual.label: Open supervisory findings at failure
visual.sub: About triple the number at peer firms
visual.src: Federal Reserve review, executive summary, Apr 2023

scenes.say: Yet the inspector general found the Fed did not downgrade the bank's overall rating until August 2022.

visual.text: SVB's supervisory ratings are downgraded
visual.src: Federal Reserve OIG, Sep 2023

scenes.say: The Fed's own review, led by its Vice Chair for Supervision, Michael Barr, was blunt about the Fed itself.

visual.text: Supervisors did not fully appreciate the extent of the vulnerabilities as Silicon Valley Bank grew in size and complexity.
visual.src: Federal Reserve review, executive summary, Apr 2023

scenes.say: And when supervisors did find problems, the review said, they did not take sufficient steps to make sure the bank fixed them quickly enough.

visual.text: did not take sufficient steps to ensure that Silicon Valley Bank fixed those problems quickly enough.
visual.src: Federal Reserve review, executive summary, Apr 2023

scenes.say: By early 2023, the bank had large losses on its bonds, a concentrated customer base, and almost all of its deposits uninsured. It only needed a spark.

visual.text: All it needed was a spark

scenes.say: On the eighth of March 2023, the group announced a plan to shore up its finances.

visual.text: Forty-eight hours

scenes.say: It had sold 21 billion dollars of securities, booking a 1.8 billion dollar loss after tax. It planned to increase its borrowing by 15 to 30 billion dollars, and to raise 2.25 billion dollars of new capital.

visual.title: The 8 March announcement
visual.src: Federal Reserve review, executive summary, Apr 2023

scenes.say: The inspector general later found that management's ineffective public communications about that plan contributed to the deposit outflows.

visual.text: management's ineffective public communications of its plan to raise additional capital
visual.src: Federal Reserve OIG, Sep 2023

scenes.say: Government deposit insurance covers 250,000 dollars per depositor, per bank, for each ownership category. Above that, there is no guarantee.

visual.label: FDIC deposit insurance limit
visual.sub: Per depositor, per bank, per ownership category
visual.src: FDIC

scenes.say: At Silicon Valley Bank, most deposits sat above that line. The Fed's 2023 review described depositors who, fuelled by social media, withdrew uninsured deposits in a coordinated manner.

visual.text: fueled by social media, withdrew uninsured deposits in a coordinated manner
visual.src: Federal Reserve review, executive summary, Apr 2023

scenes.say: On the ninth of March, more than 40 billion dollars left the bank.

visual.label: Withdrawn on 9 March 2023
visual.src: Federal Reserve review, executive summary, Apr 2023

scenes.say: For comparison, the review noted that in 2008, Wachovia lost about 10 billion dollars over eight days, and Washington Mutual 19 billion over 16 days.

visual.title: Deposit outflows in bank runs
visual.src: Federal Reserve review, executive summary, Apr 2023

scenes.say: And for the next day, management expected more than 100 billion dollars of further withdrawals.

visual.label: Further withdrawals expected on 10 March
visual.src: Federal Reserve review, executive summary, Apr 2023

scenes.say: On the tenth of March, California's Department of Financial Protection and Innovation closed Silicon Valley Bank.

visual.title: Silicon Valley Bank
lines: Bank closed by the state regulator
visual.src: Federal Reserve review, executive summary, Apr 2023

scenes.say: Two days later, on the twelfth of March, state regulators also closed Signature Bank.

visual.text: Signature Bank is closed too
visual.src: Treasury, Fed and FDIC joint statement, 12 Mar 2023

scenes.say: That Sunday evening, the Treasury, the Federal Reserve and the FDIC issued a joint statement.

visual.text: Who paid

scenes.say: Depositors, it said, would have access to all of their money starting Monday, the thirteenth of March. That included deposits above the insurance limit.

visual.text: all of their money starting Monday, March 13.
visual.by: Treasury, Federal Reserve and FDIC, 12 March 2023
visual.src: Treasury, Fed and FDIC joint statement, 12 Mar 2023

scenes.say: And, the agencies said, no losses associated with the resolution of Silicon Valley Bank would be borne by the taxpayer.

visual.text: No losses associated with the resolution of Silicon Valley Bank will be borne by the taxpayer.
visual.src: Treasury, Fed and FDIC joint statement, 12 Mar 2023

scenes.say: So who did lose? Shareholders and certain unsecured debtholders were not protected. Senior management was removed.

visual.title: Not protected
visual.src: Treasury, Fed and FDIC joint statement, 12 Mar 2023

scenes.say: On the seventeenth of March, the parent company, SVB Financial Group, filed for bankruptcy.

visual.text: SVB Financial Group files for bankruptcy
visual.src: Federal Reserve review, Apr 2023

scenes.say: Over that weekend and the days after, the FDIC ran the business as a temporary bridge bank. As of the tenth of March, it had about 167 billion dollars of assets and about 119 billion dollars of deposits.

visual.src: FDIC press release, Mar 2023

scenes.say: A buyer emerged. First Citizens bought about 72 billion dollars of the failed bank's assets, at a discount of 16.5 billion dollars. About 90 billion dollars of securities and other assets stayed with the FDIC.

visual.src: FDIC press release, Mar 2023

scenes.say: The 17 former branches reopened under the First Citizens name on the twenty-seventh of March. The FDIC estimated the cost to its Deposit Insurance Fund at about 20 billion dollars.

visual.label: Estimated cost to the Deposit Insurance Fund
visual.sub: FDIC estimate, March 2023; final figure set when the receivership ends
visual.src: FDIC press release, Mar 2023

scenes.say: Of the cost of the SVB and Signature failures, about 16.3 billion dollars came from protecting uninsured depositors. The FDIC decided that banks would pay it back, through a special assessment.

visual.title: Special assessment
lines: !About $16.3bn of losses from protecting uninsured depositors (SVB and Signature)
visual.src: FDIC special assessment final rule, Nov 2023

scenes.say: Banking organisations with less than 5 billion dollars of assets would pay nothing. So the bill for protecting uninsured depositors went to the larger banks.

visual.label: Banking organisations expected to pay
visual.src: FDIC special assessment final rule, Nov 2023

scenes.say: In April 2023, the Federal Reserve published its own review, along with more than two dozen documents of confidential supervisory information.

visual.text: Two verdicts

scenes.say: It named four causes. The board and management failed to manage their risks. Supervisors did not fully appreciate the vulnerabilities. They did not act quickly enough. And the Board's tailoring rules, together with a shift in supervisory policy, had reduced standards and promoted a less assertive approach.

visual.title: The Fed's four takeaways, 2023
items: Board and management failed to manage risks
Supervisors did not fully appreciate the vulnerabilities
Problems were not fixed quickly enough
Tailoring rules and a policy shift: lower standards
visual.src: Federal Reserve review, executive summary, Apr 2023

scenes.say: Michael Barr wrote that the Fed must strengthen its supervision and regulation based on what it had learned.

visual.text: we must strengthen the Federal Reserve's supervision and regulation based on what we have learned.
visual.by: Michael Barr, Fed Vice Chair for Supervision, 28 Apr 2023
visual.src: Federal Reserve press release, 28 Apr 2023

scenes.say: In September 2026, a second account arrived. Fed Vice Chair for Supervision Michelle Bowman described the first, preliminary findings of an independent review by the Starling Advisory Group.

visual.text: A second review
visual.sub: Preliminary findings by the Starling Advisory Group
visual.src: Fed Vice Chair Bowman on independent review, Sep 2026

scenes.say: It found that staff knew, or should have known, about the bank's vulnerabilities as early as March 2022, and did not take prompt and decisive action to get the bank to reduce its interest-rate risk.

visual.text: When staff knew, or should have known
visual.src: Fed Vice Chair Bowman on independent review, Sep 2026

scenes.say: But on two points, it pointed in a different direction. It found the delays were not caused by the regulatory tailoring rules, or by any directive from the Fed's former Vice Chair for Supervision.

visual.title: What the 2026 review says did not cause the delays
items: Any directive from the former Vice Chair for Supervision
visual.src: Fed Vice Chair Bowman on independent review, Sep 2026

scenes.say: Instead, it pointed to culture. Staff, it found, believed it was personally safer to take no action unless they were certain the action was exactly right.

visual.text: it was personally safer to take no action unless they were certain the action was exactly right.
visual.by: Independent review (preliminary), per Michelle Bowman, Sep 2026
visual.src: Fed Vice Chair Bowman on independent review, Sep 2026

scenes.say: And on social media, it reached a different conclusion. An analysis for the review found that 96 per cent of the relevant online chatter appeared after the bank's failure was already inevitable.

visual.label: of relevant chatter came after failure was inevitable
visual.sub: Charles River Associates analysis for the independent review
visual.src: Fed Vice Chair Bowman on independent review, Sep 2026

scenes.say: So the 2023 review said social media fuelled the run. The 2026 findings say social media did not trigger it, and found no evidence it accelerated it. One is the Fed's own review. The other is the preliminary findings of an independent review. They do not agree.

visual.text: Two reviews. Two answers.
visual.sub: 2023: fuelled by social media. 2026: did not trigger it; no evidence it accelerated it.

scenes.say: Bowman said the Fed had already issued a statement of supervisory operating principles, without waiting for the review. She also announced monthly escalation reports from examination teams to the heads of supervision and their Reserve Banks.

visual.title: The Fed's 2026 changes
items: Supervisory Operating Principles (issued before the review)
New: monthly escalation reports from examination teams
visual.src: Fed Vice Chair Bowman on independent review, Sep 2026

scenes.say: So what does the record actually show?

visual.text: What the paperwork shows

scenes.say: Set the arguments aside, and the documents agree on the basics. A bank that grew very fast. Deposits concentrated in one industry, almost all of them uninsured. A large bet on long-dated bonds, with the hedges removed. And warnings that were not acted on quickly enough.

visual.title: Where the records agree
items: A large bet on long-dated bonds
Warnings not acted on quickly enough

scenes.say: Our reading is that the run was the last step, not the cause. The losses that made the bank fragile were, the latest review says, visible to supervisors a year earlier.

visual.text: The run was the last step, not the cause.

scenes.say: Three lessons stand out. For businesses: know how much of your cash is actually insured. For banks: depositors who think alike can leave together. For supervisors: finding a problem is not the same as fixing it.

visual.title: Three lessons
items: Businesses: know how much of your cash is insured
Banks: depositors who think alike can leave together
Supervisors: finding a problem is not fixing it

scenes.say: Silicon Valley Bank took 40 years to build. It took two days to fall. And the warning signs, the records show, were on file long before the run began.

visual.text: 40 years to build. Two days to fall.

visual.text: Subscribe for the next case file
